entries.clinician_note: A no-frills slide viewer. Opens big scanner files quickly and lets you draw regions.
entries.name: ASAP
entries.tagline: Fast whole-slide image viewer with annotation support.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Lightweight viewer for multi-resolution whole-slide images with a simple annotation workflow, widely used to inspect and label slides for challenge datasets.

entries.clinician_note: Research-focused. Useful if you want the academic papers rather than usable tools.
entries.name: Awesome-Pathology-VLMs
entries.tagline: Curated list of pathology vision-language models, datasets and benchmarks.
entries.summary: Focused bibliography of pathology vision-language models organised by training paradigm, with a useful patch/ROI/WSI granularity axis. A good deep reference for the VLM literature specifically.

entries.name: CAMELYON16
entries.tagline: Lymph node metastasis detection challenge dataset.
entries.summary: Sentinel lymph node whole-slide images with exhaustive metastasis annotations. The reference benchmark for weakly and fully supervised WSI detection.

entries.name: CellViT
entries.tagline: Vision-transformer nucleus segmentation and classification.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Transformer-based nucleus instance segmentation built on pretrained ViT encoders, with inference tooling for scaling detection across whole slides.

entries.name: CLAM
entries.tagline: Attention-based multiple-instance learning for weakly supervised whole-slide classification.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Widely used reference implementation of attention-based MIL for slide-level classification from slide-level labels only, with heatmap interpretability. The default baseline in most WSI classification papers.

entries.licence_notes: Gated on Hugging Face; non-commercial research terms.
entries.name: CONCH
entries.tagline: Vision-language foundation model for pathology image-text tasks.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Contrastively pretrained image-text model for pathology supporting zero-shot classification, cross-modal retrieval, captioning and segmentation.

entries.clinician_note: Runs on a server your institution controls, so several people can annotate the same slides in a browser. Needs IT support to set up.
entries.caveats: Self-hosting requires a server and maintenance; not a laptop tool.
entries.name: Cytomine
entries.tagline: Web-based collaborative platform for annotating and analysing whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Server-hosted platform for multi-user slide annotation, review and analysis, designed for collaborative projects and teaching cohorts.

entries.licence_notes: Open standard published by NEMA; the specification is free to read.
entries.clinician_note: The reason a slide from one scanner can be opened by another vendor's software. Ask about DICOM support before buying anything.
entries.name: DICOM for Whole Slide Imaging
entries.tagline: The vendor-neutral standard for storing and exchanging pathology slides.
entries.summary: The DICOM VL Whole Slide Microscopy Image IOD defines how scanned slides are represented, enabling storage and exchange independent of scanner vendor.

entries.name: Digital Slide Archive
entries.tagline: Server platform for managing, annotating and analysing large slide collections.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Web platform built on Girder for organising whole-slide image collections, with annotation tooling and a plugin system for running analysis jobs at scale.

entries.licence_notes: Aggregates many source datasets, each with its own terms.
entries.name: HEST-1k / HEST-Bench
entries.tagline: Paired histology and spatial transcriptomics dataset and benchmark.
entries.summary: Harmonised collection of spatial transcriptomics profiles paired with histology, plus a benchmark for predicting expression from morphology.

entries.name: HistomicsTK
entries.tagline: Python toolkit for histology image analysis and feature extraction.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Library of histology-specific image analysis routines — colour deconvolution, stain normalisation, nucleus detection and morphometric feature extraction — usable standalone or as the analysis layer behind Digital Slide Archive.

entries.clinician_note: Checks a batch of scanned slides for problems like blur or pen marks before anyone spends time on them.
entries.name: HistoQC
entries.tagline: Automated quality control for whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Pipeline that flags slide artefacts — blur, pen marks, tissue folds, coverslip edges, bubbles — and produces an interactive report for triaging a cohort before analysis.

entries.name: HoVer-Net
entries.tagline: Simultaneous nucleus segmentation and classification in histology.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Network predicting horizontal and vertical distances to nuclear centres to separate touching nuclei, while simultaneously classifying nucleus type. A standard baseline for nucleus tasks.

entries.clinician_note: A good starting dataset if you are learning — small enough to work with on a laptop.
entries.name: NCT-CRC-HE-100K
entries.tagline: Colorectal tissue-type patch classification dataset.
entries.summary: Around 100,000 colorectal H&E patches labelled into nine tissue classes. Small, permissively licensed and CPU-tractable, which makes it the usual first dataset for teaching and prototyping.

entries.name: OMERO
entries.tagline: Image data management server for microscopy, including whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Long-established server and client suite for storing, annotating and sharing microscopy image data across many proprietary formats.

entries.name: OpenSlide
entries.tagline: C library with Python bindings for reading proprietary whole-slide formats.
entries.summary: The foundational library for reading vendor whole-slide formats (Aperio, Hamamatsu, Leica, MIRAX and others) through one common interface. Most Python pathology tooling depends on it.

entries.licence_notes: Kaggle competition terms apply; check before redistribution.
entries.name: PANDA
entries.tagline: Prostate biopsy Gleason grading challenge dataset.
entries.summary: The largest public prostate biopsy collection with Gleason grade labels, from two institutions, used to benchmark automated grading against pathologist variability.

entries.name: PanNuke
entries.tagline: Pan-cancer nucleus instance segmentation and classification dataset.
entries.licence_notes: Non-commercial research licence — check the terms before any commercial use.
entries.caveats: Nucleus class definitions are coarse and were produced semi-automatically then refined; treat per-class performance figures with corresponding caution.
entries.summary: Nucleus instance segmentation and classification dataset spanning 19 tissue types with five nucleus classes, semi-automatically annotated. One of the standard training and evaluation sets for nucleus models.

maintainers: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute AI Operations & Data Science
entries.name: PathML
entries.tagline: Python library for computational pathology preprocessing and modelling.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Framework for building reproducible pathology pipelines, with support for brightfield, multiparametric and volumetric imaging and a preprocessing DSL.

entries.name: Patho-Bench
entries.tagline: Standardised evaluation suite for pathology slide-level foundation models.
entries.summary: Harness for comparing slide-level foundation models across many public tasks under consistent splits and protocols, reducing the incomparability of self-reported numbers.

entries.licence_notes: Free to read; content is copyrighted by the publisher.
entries.clinician_note: Not an AI tool, but the reference most pathologists already use — included because AI outputs should always be checked against a trusted source.
entries.name: PathologyOutlines
entries.tagline: Free comprehensive online pathology reference.
entries.summary: Widely used free reference covering diagnostic criteria, immunohistochemistry and differentials across pathology, maintained by a large contributor network.

entries.licence_notes: Openly licensed — unusual among pathology foundation models and worth preferring where it performs comparably.
entries.clinician_note: Notable because it is genuinely open — no access request, no non-commercial restriction.
entries.name: Phikon-v2
entries.tagline: Openly licensed pathology tile encoder trained on public cohorts.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: ViT trained with DINOv2 on public histopathology cohorts and released under a permissive licence, making it one of the few pathology encoders usable without gated access.

entries.licence_notes: Check the model card and the OpenPath data terms before reuse.
entries.caveats: Training data provenance is social media; coverage and label quality vary by subspecialty.
entries.name: PLIP
entries.tagline: Pathology CLIP model trained on image-text pairs mined from social media.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: CLIP fine-tuned on the OpenPath corpus of pathology image-text pairs curated from public medical Twitter, enabling zero-shot classification and image-text retrieval.

entries.licence_notes: Gated on Hugging Face; non-commercial research terms apply.
entries.name: Prov-GigaPath
entries.tagline: Slide-level foundation model with a tile encoder and long-context aggregator.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Pairs a tile-level encoder with a LongNet-based slide aggregator so whole slides can be represented in one pass, evaluated on subtyping and mutation prediction.

entries.licence_notes: Derived from third-party video content; review the terms before redistribution.
entries.name: Quilt-1M
entries.tagline: Histopathology image-text pairs mined from educational videos.
entries.summary: Large open histopathology image-caption corpus assembled from educational videos, used to train pathology vision-language models.

entries.licence_notes: Check model and dataset cards; derived from third-party video content.
entries.name: Quilt-LLaVA
entries.tagline: Instruction-tuned pathology assistant trained from educational video narration.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Multimodal assistant instruction-tuned on localised narratives extracted from open histopathology teaching videos, aimed at diagnostic reasoning across patches.

entries.clinician_note: Free, installs on an ordinary laptop, and does not upload your slides anywhere. The usual first stop if you have never used digital pathology software.
entries.caveats: Not a diagnostic device. Very large slides benefit from more RAM.
entries.name: QuPath
entries.tagline: Open-source desktop software for whole-slide image analysis and annotation.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Cross-platform desktop application for whole-slide and microscopy image analysis, with scripting, an extension system, and strong annotation tooling. The de facto open-source starting point for digital pathology.

entries.clinician_note: Another automatic cell-detection option inside QuPath. Needs a one-time Python setup.
entries.caveats: Requires a working local Cellpose environment; setup is the fiddly part.
entries.name: QuPath Cellpose Extension
entries.tagline: Brings Cellpose and Omnipose segmentation into QuPath.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Community extension that calls a local Cellpose/Omnipose install from QuPath, adding generalist cell segmentation models to the QuPath workflow.

entries.clinician_note: Newer segmentation option that runs without a graphics card.
entries.name: QuPath InstanSeg Extension
entries.tagline: InstanSeg nucleus and cell segmentation inside QuPath.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Extension exposing InstanSeg, an embedding-based instance segmentation method, with bundled models runnable on CPU directly from QuPath.

entries.clinician_note: Adds automatic nucleus detection to QuPath. Runs on a normal laptop, no coding needed.
entries.name: QuPath StarDist Extension
entries.tagline: Runs StarDist star-convex nucleus detection inside QuPath.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Official QuPath extension wrapping StarDist, giving point-and-click nucleus segmentation on H&E, IHC and fluorescence images without writing code.

entries.name: Slideflow
entries.tagline: End-to-end deep learning pipeline for whole-slide images.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Opinionated pipeline covering tessellation, training, MIL, explainability and deployment, with both TensorFlow and PyTorch backends and a slide viewer.

entries.name: StarDist
entries.tagline: Star-convex polygon nucleus detection.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Instance segmentation method representing nuclei as star-convex polygons, robust on crowded nuclei and the basis of the most-used QuPath segmentation extension.

entries.licence_notes: Open and controlled-access tiers; controlled data requires dbGaP authorisation.
entries.caveats: Tissue-source-site signal is a well-documented confounder — split by site, not just by patient, or results inflate.
entries.name: TCGA
entries.tagline: Pan-cancer whole-slide and molecular data archive.
entries.summary: The most widely used public source of paired whole-slide images and molecular data across cancer types, underpinning most published WSI classification, survival and biomarker work.

entries.name: TIAToolbox
entries.tagline: Python toolbox for computational pathology pipelines.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Batteries-included Python library covering slide reading, stain normalisation, patch extraction, pretrained models and end-to-end inference pipelines.

entries.licence_notes: Gated on Hugging Face; research terms apply.
entries.name: TITAN
entries.tagline: Multimodal whole-slide foundation model producing slide-level embeddings.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Slide-level model combining visual self-supervision with vision-language alignment, giving whole-slide embeddings usable without task-specific training.

entries.name: TRIDENT
entries.tagline: Toolkit for whole-slide preprocessing and foundation-model feature extraction.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Pipeline for tissue segmentation, patching and batch feature extraction across many pathology foundation models behind one interface.

entries.licence_notes: Access is gated on Hugging Face and the licence restricts commercial use. Read the terms before any non-research application.
entries.caveats: Gated weights with a non-commercial licence. Trained on a corpus that is not public, so independent replication is limited.
entries.name: UNI
entries.tagline: Self-supervised vision foundation model for pathology tile encoding.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: ViT encoder trained with DINOv2 on a large private histopathology corpus, used as a frozen tile-level feature extractor across a wide range of downstream tasks.

entries.licence_notes: Gated on Hugging Face; check the model card for permitted use.
entries.caveats: Industry-released with gated access; the training corpus is not public.
entries.name: Virchow2
entries.tagline: Large pathology vision foundation model trained on a very large slide corpus.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Vision transformer trained self-supervised on a very large multi-institutional slide collection, released for research as a general-purpose tile encoder.

entries.name: WSInfer
entries.tagline: Runs pretrained patch classification models across whole slides, with a QuPath front end.

regulatory.detail: Research use only. Not for primary diagnosis.

entries.summary: Toolkit and model zoo for running patch-level deep learning inference over whole-slide images, usable from the command line or through a QuPath extension.
